translation_en: Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to me: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Yala ibn Ata, from Abu Alqamah, who said: Abu Hurayrah narrated to me directly: I heard the Messenger of Allah... [Another chain:] Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to me: My father narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us. Both said: Shubah narrated to us, from Yala ibn Ata, who heard Abu Alqamah, who heard Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like theirs.
Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Mamar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like theirs.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Haywah, that Abu Yunus, the freedman of Abu Hurayrah, narrated to him: I heard Abu Hurayrah report this from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Whoever obeys the commander... He did not say 'my commander.' The same wording is in Hammam's hadith from Abu Hurayrah.

Said ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us, both from Yaqoub. Said said: Yaqoub ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: You must listen and obey in hardship and ease, when eager and reluctant, and even when others are given preference over you.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ashari, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us. They said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Shubah, from Abu Imran, from Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: My close companion advised me to listen and obey, even if the appointed leader were a slave mutilated in his limbs.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq informed us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us. All report it from Shubah, from Abu Imran, with this chain, and both said: 'an Abyssinian slave, mutilated in his limbs.'
Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated this to us: My father narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Imran, with this chain, as Ibn Idris said: 'a slave mutilated in his limbs.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Husayn, who said: I heard my grandmother narrate that she heard the Prophet deliver a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, saying: Even if a slave is appointed over you and leads you by the Book of Allah, listen to him and obey him.
Ibn Bashshar narrated this to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shubah, with this chain, and he said: 'an Abyssinian slave.'
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Shubah, with this chain, and he said: 'a mutilated Abyssinian slave.'

Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, with this chain. He did not mention 'Abyssinian' or 'mutilated,' and added that she heard the Messenger of Allah at Mina or Arafat.

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn Ayan narrated to us: Maqil narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Yahya ibn Husayn, from his grandmother Umm al-Husayn, who said: I performed the Farewell Pilgrimage with the Messenger of Allah. She said: The Messenger of Allah spoke at length, then I heard him say: If a mutilated slave is placed in authority over you—I think she said, a black man—who leads you by the Book of Allah, listen to him and obey him.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, who said: A Muslim must listen and obey in what he likes and dislikes, unless he is commanded to commit an act of disobedience. If he is commanded to disobey Allah, then there is no listening and no obedience.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us: Yahya (al-Qattan) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us. Both report it from Ubaydullah with this chain and a similar wording.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Sad ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, that the Prophet sent out an army and appointed a man over them. The man lit a fire and said: Enter it. Some wanted to enter, while others said: We have fled from it. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, and he said to those who wanted to enter: Had you entered it, you would have remained in it until the Day of Resurrection. He said something good to the others and said: There is no obedience in disobedience to Allah. Obedience is only in what is right.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Said al-Ashajj narrated to us; their wordings are close. They said: Waki narrated to us: al-Amash narrated to us, from Sad ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah sent out a detachment and appointed an Ansari man over them, instructing them to listen to him and obey him. They angered him over something, so he said: Gather firewood for me. They gathered it. Then he said: Light a fire. They lit it. He said: Did the Messenger of Allah not order you to listen to me and obey me? They said: Yes. He said: Then enter it. They looked at one another and said: We fled from the Fire to the Messenger of Allah. They remained like that until his anger subsided and the fire went out. When they returned, they told the Prophet about it. He said: Had they entered it, they would not have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki and Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-Amash, with this chain and a similar report.

Ibrahim narrated from Muslim, who said: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Warqa narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: The imam is a shield; fighting is done behind him and protection is sought through him. If he commands mindfulness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and acts justly, he will have a reward for that. If he commands otherwise, it will be against him.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu Hazim, who said: I kept company with Abu Hurayrah for five years and heard him narrate from the Prophet, who said: The Children of Israel were governed by prophets. Whenever a prophet died, another prophet succeeded him. There will be no prophet after me, but there will be many caliphs. They asked: What do you command us to do? He said: Fulfill the pledge of allegiance to the first one and then the next, and give them their due, for Allah will ask them about those He placed under their care.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ashari said: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Furat, from his father, with this chain and a similar report.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas and Waki narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Said al-Ashajj narrated to me: Waki narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Kurayb and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ali ibn Khashram said: Isa ibn Yunus informed us. All of them report it from al-Amash. [Another chain, in this wording:] Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: After me, there will be others given preference and matters you will disapprove of. They said: Messenger of Allah, what do you command those of us who live to see that? He said: Fulfill the duty that is upon you, and ask Allah for what is due to you.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ishaq said: He informed us; Zuhayr said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Rabb al-Kabah, who said: I entered the mosque and found Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As sitting in the shade of the Ka'bah, with people gathered around him. I went over and sat with them. He said: We were traveling with the Messenger of Allah. We stopped at a place; some of us were repairing our tents, some were practicing archery, and some were tending their livestock. Then the caller of the Messenger of Allah called: The prayer is gathering. We gathered around the Messenger of Allah, and he said: There was no prophet before me except that it was his duty to guide his community to the best he knew for them and warn them of the worst he knew for them. The well-being of this community has been placed in its early period, and its later period will be afflicted by trials and matters you will disapprove of. A trial will come, and each one will make the next seem lighter. A trial will come, and the believer will say: This one will destroy me. Then it will pass. Another trial will come, and the believer will say: This one, this one. Whoever wishes to be moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, let death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would like them to treat him. Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader, giving him his hand and the sincerity of his heart, should obey him as much as he is able. If another comes to challenge him, strike the neck of the latter. I came near him and said: I adjure you by Allah: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah? He put his hands to his ears and heart and said: My ears heard it and my heart retained it. I said: This cousin of yours, Muawiyah, orders us to consume one another's wealth wrongfully and to kill one another, while Allah says: 'O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth wrongfully, but only through trade by mutual consent, and do not kill yourselves. Surely Allah is ever Merciful to you.' (Quran 4:29) He was silent for a while, then said: Obey him in obedience to Allah, and disobey him in disobedience to Allah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, and Abu Said al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us. Both report it from al-Amash with this chain and a similar account.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Abu al-Mundhir Ismail ibn Umar narrated to us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar narrated to us, from Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Rabb al-Kabah al-Saidi, who said: I saw a group gathered by the Ka'bah. He mentioned a report like al-Amash's hadith.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah narrate from Anas ibn Malik, from Usayd ibn Hudayr, that a man from the Ansar spoke privately with the Messenger of Allah and said: Will you not appoint me as you appointed so-and-so? He said: After me, you will encounter others being given preference, so be patient until you meet me at the Pool.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to me: Khalid (Ibn al-Harith) narrated to us: Shubah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas narrate from Usayd ibn Hudayr that a man from the Ansar spoke privately with the Messenger of Allah, with a report like it. Ubaydullah ibn Muadh also narrated it to me: My father narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us with this chain, but did not say that the man spoke privately with the Messenger of Allah.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Alqamah ibn Wail al-Hadrami, from his father, who said: Salamah ibn Yazid al-Jufi asked the Messenger of Allah: Prophet of Allah, what do you advise us if rulers demand their rights from us but deny us our rights? He turned away from him. He asked again, and the Prophet turned away. When he asked a second or third time, al-Ashath ibn Qays pulled him aside, and the Prophet said: Listen and obey. They are responsible for what they have been charged with, and you are responsible for what you have been charged with.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Shababah narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Simak, with this chain and a similar report. It says that al-Ashath ibn Qays pulled him aside, then the Messenger of Allah said: Listen and obey. They are responsible for what they have been charged with, and you are responsible for what you have been charged with.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me: Busr ibn Ubaydullah al-Hadrami narrated to me that he heard Abu Idris al-Khawlani say: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: People used to ask the Messenger of Allah about good, while I asked him about evil, fearing it might reach me. I said: Messenger of Allah, we were in ignorance and evil, then Allah brought us this good. Will there be evil after this good? He said: Yes. I asked: Will there be good after that evil? He said: Yes, but it will be tainted. I asked: What is its taint? He said: People who follow a way other than my way and guide by something other than my guidance. You will recognize some of what they do and disapprove of some. I asked: Will there be evil after that good? He said: Yes, callers at the gates of Hell. Whoever responds to them, they will throw him into it. I said: Messenger of Allah, describe them to us. He said: They will be people from our own community, speaking our language. I asked: What do you advise if I live to see that? He said: Stay with the body of the Muslims and their leader. I asked: If they have neither a community nor a leader? He said: Then keep away from all those factions, even if you must bite the root of a tree, until death comes to you while you are in that state.

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar al-Tamimi narrated to me: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us: Yahya (Ibn Hassan) narrated to us: Muawiyah (Ibn Sallam) narrated to us: Zayd ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Abu Sallam, who said: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: I asked: Messenger of Allah, we were in evil, then Allah brought good, and we are in it. Will there be evil beyond this good? He said: Yes. I asked: Will there be good beyond that evil? He said: Yes. I asked: Will there be evil beyond that good? He said: Yes. I asked: How? He said: After me there will be leaders who are not guided by my guidance and do not follow my way. Some men will arise among them whose hearts are the hearts of devils in human bodies. I asked: Messenger of Allah, what should I do if I live to see that? He said: Listen and obey the ruler, even if your back is struck and your property is taken. Listen and obey.
